scenes.headline: Your money can earn money
scenes.narration: Most people think interest is a small bonus. Over a long enough time, it can become the biggest part of your savings.

scenes.headline: Interest earns interest
scenes.narration: With compound interest, each year's earnings are added to your balance. Next year, you earn interest on that bigger amount.

scenes.headline: A simple example
scenes.narration: Say you invest one thousand dollars at five percent a year and leave it alone. The numbers below are round figures, for illustration only.

scenes.headline: Simple vs compound, 30 years
scenes.narration: After ten years, the compound balance is about sixteen hundred dollars. Simple interest gives fifteen hundred. The gap keeps growing.
scenes.body: Example only: $1,000 at 5% a year, no extra deposits.

scenes.headline: Time does the heavy lifting
scenes.narration: The earlier you start, the more years interest has to compound. In this example, doubling the years more than doubles the growth.

scenes.headline: Regular deposits speed it up
scenes.narration: Adding a fixed amount every month gives compounding more to work with. Your balance grows faster than it would from one deposit alone.

scenes.headline: Fees compound against you
scenes.narration: Fees and high-interest debt compound too, but they work against you. Check what you pay before you invest.

scenes.headline: Start with what you can
scenes.narration: You do not need a large sum to begin. Start small, stay steady, and let time do its work. This is general information, not financial advice.
